  MINUTES
  VERNON CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  TUESDAY, MAY 19, 2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Ybarra called the meeting to order at 9:44 a.m.

  FLAG SALUTE

  Mayor Ybarra led the Flag Salute during the County Sanitation District No. 23 meeting,
  which was held immediately before the City Council meeting.

  ROLL CALL

  APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA

  approve the agenda. The question was called and the motion carried 4-0, Council

  PUBLIC COMMENT
  None.

  PRESENTATIONS
  1.  Employee Service Pin Awards
  Recommendation: Recognize April 2026 Employee Service Pin Award recipients.

  Human Resources Director Tan presented the item, and the City Council
  recognized the April 2026 Employee Service Pin Award recipients: Utilities
  Operations Manager, Jared Dacey and Management Analyst, John Lau, based on
  the number of service years with the City of Vernon.

  2.  National Public Works Week Proclamation
  Recommendation: Recognize the week of May 17 - 23, 2026 as National Public
  Works Week in the City of Vernon.

  Public Works Director Wall read the proclamation, and the City Council recognized
  the week of May 17 - 23, 2026 as National Public Works Week in the City of
  Vernon. Mayor Ybarra on behalf of the City Council presented the proclamation to
  Cynthia Cano and Eli Zepeda.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Ybarra inquired whether the City Council wished to pull any items from the
  Consent Calendar, and Mayor Ybarra noted that she wished to pull item No. 11 for
  more information.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra, called
  for a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar with the exception of agenda Item No. 11. The
  question was called and the motion carried 4-0, with Council Member Merlo
  absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  3.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the May 5, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
  Minutes.
  4.  Claims Against the City
  Recommendation: Receive and file the claim submitted by Jennifer De Anda
  Plascencia.

  5.  Operating Account Warrant Register
  Recommendation: Approve Operating Account Warrant Register No. 173, for the
  period of April 5, 2026 through April 18, 2026, totaling $12,038,189.03 and
  consisting of ratification of electronic payments totaling $11,932,922.26 and
  ratification of the issuance of early checks totaling $105,266.77.
  6.  Fire Department Activity Reports
  Recommendation: Receive and file the February and March 2026 Fire Department
  Activity Reports.
  7.  Police Department Activity Report
  Recommendation: Receive and file the March 2026 Police Department Activity
  Report.
  8.  Purchase Order with AT&T for VESTA 9-1-1 System Maintenance
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize issuance of a Purchase Order to AT&T
  for an amount not-to-exceed $23,776.11, for a one-year term extension of the
  Support Agreement for the VESTA 9-1-1 system from April 16, 2026 to April 15,
  2027.
  9.  Project Funded by Senate Bill 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act of
  2017 for Fiscal Year 2026-27
  Recommendation: A. Find that the approval of the proposed resolution does not
  constitute a "project" pursuant to sections 15378(b)(2) and (4) of the Guidelines to
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), because it constitutes an
  administrative activity and government funding mechanism that does not involve
  any commitment to any specific project which may result in a potentially significant
  impact on the environment; and even if the adoption of the proposed resolution did
  constitute a project, it would be exempt from CEQA in accordance with Section
  15061(b)(3), the general rule that CEQA only applies to projects that may have a
  significant effect on the environment; and B. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-022
  adopting a project list to be funded by Senate Bill 1: The Road Repair and
  Accountability Act of 2017 for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27.
  10.  Contract with R Dependable Const Inc. for Vernon City Hall Third Floor
  Facilities Renovations
  Recommendation: A. Find that the proposed action is categorically exempt from
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review, in accordance with CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15301, because the project consists of the maintenance, repair
  or minor alteration of existing facilities and equipment and involves negligible or no
  expansion of an existing or former use; B. Accept the bid proposal from R
  Dependable Const Inc. as the most responsive and responsible bidder for the
  Vernon City Hall Third Floor Facilities Renovations project and reject all other bids;
  C. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute Contract No. 20260210
  in the amount of $126,000.00 for the Vernon City Hall Third Floor Facilities
  Renovations project for a period not to exceed 90 days; and D. Authorize a
  contingency amount of ten percent (10%) or $12,600.00 in the event of an
  unexpected changed condition in the project and grant authority to the City
  Administrator to issue a change order(s) for an amount up to the contingency
  amount, if necessary.

  The following item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for individual
  consideration:

  11.  Services Agreement with Hafenfeld Ranch, LLC.
  Recommendation: A. Find that it is in the best interests of the City to award a
  contract directly to Hafenfeld Ranch, LLC without a competitive selection process,
  based on their existing operational presence in Kern County and unique
  combination of services offered, pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Section
  3.32.110(B)(2); B. Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), in accordance with the common-sense
  exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), because it can be seen
  with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a
  significant effect on the environment. Further environmental review, if required
  under CEQA, will be performed prior to approval of any activity that has the
  potential for causing a significant effect on the environment; C. Approve and
  authorize the City Administrator to execute the Services Agreement with Hafenfeld
  Ranch, LLC (Hafenfeld Ranch), in substantially the same form as submitted, to
  provide consulting, infrastructure, and construction services in an amount not-to-
  exceed $600,000 for a three-year term; and D. Authorize a contingency amount of
  ten percent (10%) or $60,000 in the event of unforeseen expenses, including
  surcharges, price volatility, and additional work, and grant authority to the City
  Administrator to approve and execute amendments up to the contingency amount,
  if necessary.

  Public Utilities General Manager Dusenberry presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra asked how long Hafenfeld Ranch has been using the Kern County
  property.

  Public Utilities General Manager Dusenberry clarified that Hafenfeld owns a ranch
  nearby and grazes their cattle on the City’s property. He mentioned that the City is
  extending the agreement to cover the grazing rights and will designate Hafenfeld
  as the caretaker of the property.

  City Attorney Moussa-Milward noted that the grazing contract with Hafenfeld
  Ranch is based on a separate license agreement.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called for
  a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Rivera moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A, B, C, and D. The question was called and the motion
  carried 4-0, Council Member Merlo absent.

  NEW BUSINESS
  12.  Fiscal Year 2026-27 Budget Workshop I
  Recommendation: Conduct a workshop and provide direction to staff on the Fiscal
  Year (FY) 2026-27 estimated revenues and proposed expenditures in preparation
  for the FY 2026-27 Citywide Budget.

  City Administrator Saeki represented the staff report, Finance Director Hui
  presented an overview of the general budget, and the executive team provided
  departmental updates.

  Mayor Ybarra asked why the City was in a deficit and not breaking even in relation
  to utility use if Prime Data had replaced Farmer John’s usage when they left and
  additional companies had come on board.

  Todd Dusenberry, Public Utilities General Manager, explained that the City had lost
  legacy load in addition to Farmer John, costs have gone up, inflation, costs of
  goods, and the City has not raised rates in the last two years.

  Mayor Ybarra inquired what percentage of the FY26/27 budget was related to the
  Strategic Plan Goals approved by the City Council, and City Administrator Saeki
  responded that staff would need to return with that information.

  City Administrator Saeki reminded the City Council of Vernon City Elementary's
  request for the School Interventionist position and requested feedback on whether
  the City Council wanted to fund it.

  Mayor Ybarra asked that staff bring back the percentage of funding the Strategic
  Goals have added to the budget before considering funding the position for Vernon
  City Elementary.

  Council Member Larios opined that the City Council could consider a compromise
  and provide partial funding for the requested position; she asked that the principal
  provide a presentation so the City Council could have more details on the position
  under consideration, and City Administrator Saeki agreed.

  Council Member Larios thanked staff for their hard work and well-balanced budget.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments and there were none.

  There was no further direction provided by the City Council.

  13.  Services Agreement with Superior Management and Realty Services, Inc.
  for Residential Property Management Services
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize the City Administrator, as Housing
  Commission Director, to execute a Services Agreement with Superior
 Docusign Envelope ID: 08953490-36F7-8565-831E-C9ECE71C2789

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 6 of 8
  May 19, 2026

  Management and Realty Services, Inc. (Superior), in substantially the same form
  as submitted, for Residential Property Management Services for a total amount
  not-to-exceed $96,000.00, for a one (1) year term.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.
  Mayor Ybarra inquired about the housing budget, which increased to $300,000, as
  well as the management costs and the expenses for rehabilitating housing units.
  Director Wall explained that the budget covered the costs associated with
  rehabilitating vacant units. This included the anticipated rehabilitation of a housing
  unit on Fruitland, which had not been updated for a considerable time and would
  require extensive work to meet current standards. In addition, an apartment unit
  required rehabilitation.
  Finance Director Hui added that the City housing budget included a $200,000
  expenditure for two new vehicles that should have been included in the street
  maintenance division and acknowledged the budget would be updated.
  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve and authorize the City Administrator, as Housing Commission Director, to
  execute a Services Agreement with Superior Management and Realty Services,
  Inc. (Superior), in substantially the same form as submitted, for Residential
  Property Management Services for a total amount not-to-exceed $96,000.00, for
  a one (1) year term. The question was called and the motion carried 4-0, Council
  Member Merlo absent.
